notes.text:
Recognition theorem on an explicit existing-pair domain: K is complete nontrivially real-valued, with characteristic and residue characteristic zero; R=K^o and 0<|a|<1. An actual separated a-adic formal scheme has a finite affine cover B=R<T>/I, with I finitely generated, B complete and R-flat. Its residual fibre is a proper reduced nodal curve. Its generic fibre is ALREADY identified with the original smooth geometrically integral projective curve X^an. An actual formal invertible sheaf M has specified generic identification with the SAME original integral dL, where d clears denominators. EVERY residual component degree is strictly positive. Then, for sufficiently large k, M^k has finite formal global generators; their generic sections are algebraic sections of the same kdL; and M/d is exactly their zero-weight pureFS metric at EVERY original analytic point.

Elementary base-change lemma: let Z be proper flat finitely presented over a Noetherian ring S, and F invertible with H^i(Z,F)=0 for i>0. A finite affine cover has affine intersections because Z is separated over an affine base. Its bounded alternating Čech complex C^0,...,C^m has flat S-modules: coordinate rings are S-flat and F is locally free. It pulls back termwise to the Čech complex over ANY S-algebra. At the top, Z^m=C^m is flat. Higher exactness gives short exact sequences 0 -> Z^(q-1) -> C^(q-1) -> Z^q -> 0, descending to q=1. A flat quotient makes each sequence tensor-exact and its kernel flat. Thus H0=Z^0 is flat and all higher vanishing survives arbitrary tensoring. Proper Noetherian cohomology makes H0 finite, hence finitely presented flat and projective. This avoids general perfect-pushforward machinery. Higher vanishing alone for an arbitrary perfect complex is insufficient: [Z --2--> Z] in degrees -1,0 represents Z/2 and gains negative cohomology after tensoring with Z/2.

Rank one identifies a-adic and valuation topologies, giving R=lim R/a^j. Restricted series modulo a^j are polynomials: finitely many coefficients survive, and division by fixed a^j preserves restricted convergence. Each X_j is therefore flat finitely presented over R_j=R/a^j. Spec R_j has one prime, because every element b of the maximal ideal has some power in a^jR. Its nilradical need NOT have bounded nilpotence. Proper residual-fibre base change and Stacks37.3.4(8) give properness across this arbitrary thickening. Positive degrees imply residual ampleness by33.44.15; arbitrary-thickening ampleness37.3.2 gives ampleness on WHOLE X_1.

Descend the actual proper flat finitely presented polarized pair (X_1,M_1) to a finite-Z subring S of R/a. Enlarge the stage using32.10.1/3 for schemes and bundle/inverse/evaluation data,32.13.1 for properness,32.8.7 with10.168.1(3) for flatness, and32.4.15 for ampleness. Bases are affine qcqs and transition maps affine. Finite chart equations, principal overlap covers, inverse maps, transition units and cocycle equalities describe the actual finite-data gluing; preservation of properness and flatness uses the exact primary limit theorems. S is Noetherian. Relative Serre generation and vanishing30.16.1 apply THERE, never directly to R/a. A finite cover bounds cohomological degrees, giving a common high-power cutoff. The Čech lemma proves WHOLE mod-a H1(X_1,M_1^k)=0 and pulled-back finite generators.

Flatness and local freeness identify a^jM^k/a^(j+1)M^k with M_1^k by multiplication by a^j. H1=0 makes H0(M_(j+1)^k) -> H0(M_j^k) surjective. Lift the same finite family compatibly through all reductions. Local completeness and the equalizer description of global sections give actual formal global sections. In a complete local frame write them f_i. Modulo a, solve 1=sum b_i,0 f_i+a h_1. Repeat on each error. The convergent sums b_i=sum_j a^j b_i,j give 1=sum b_i f_i exactly; the remainder lies in a^N B and tends to zero. No Noetherian Nakayama assertion over R/a is needed.

The generic sections are already on original X^an and kdL. Projective FIELD H0 GAGA converts them to algebraic sections of that same bundle. The exact primary route is Fujiwara–Kato arXiv1308.4734v5 II9.4.1/2 in its printed stronger t.u. adhesive case: R is complete and a-torsion-free, K=R[1/a], and0.9.2.7/I2.1.4(2) put the base in that domain. Original X is proper finitely presented and the bundle coherent. No unknown carrier is algebraized and no broader unproved-in-text comparison case is substituted. At every analytic point, integral f_i and b_i have norms <=1, while 1=sum b_i f_i forces max_i|f_i|=1. Thus the formal metric is exactly the pureFS metric divided by kd, including supported points. Algebraic common zeros would have analytic points after a finite residue-field extension, contradicting this identity.

This proves the recognition implication with exact ordinary primary applications. It does NOT construct the pair for EVERY curve. Immediate comparison/limit/Serre units were read; recursive Gabber/Raynaud–Gruson/GFGA/Chow/flat-locus foundations were not all reconstructed. No universal curve equation follows.

notes.detailedSummary: Finite connected graphs with lengths in nonzero divisible Gamma admit rational-slope/Gamma-height approximants with positive curvature at ALL old and new vertices, even from a signed reference measure. notes.text:
Finite graph theorem, independently reconstructed: let G be finite connected, retaining loops, with lengths ell_e in a nonzero divisible Gamma subset R. Let signed vertex theta have mass V>0 and positive vertex mu have mass V. The outgoing-slope Laplacian satisfies -sum_v F(v)DeltaF(v)=sum_e(F(w)-F(v))^2/ell_e. Connectivity makes its kernel constants, so solve DeltaF=mu-theta. Loops contribute both incidences and their correct zero endpoint term.

Include ALL prescribed old vertices and preliminary loop subdivisions. Put rho=(V/k)sum_old delta_v and mu_eps=(1-eps)mu+eps rho. Every old margin is positive. Solve F_eps with a common normalization. Nonzero divisible Gamma is dense, so choose shared g_v in Gamma close to vertex values. On each oriented edge put d=g_w-g_v and c=d/ell; choose rationals q1<c<q2 close to c. The bend t=(q2 ell-d)/(q2-q1) lies in Gamma and strictly between endpoints, and q1t+q2(ell-t)=d exactly. Every cycle closes. New bend curvature is q2-q1>0. Choose the finitely many old outgoing-slope errors below the minimum margin divided by maximum valence, retaining positivity at every old vertex. Uniform error is bounded by vertex error plus ell(q2-q1). Opposite edge slopes cancel in total, giving raw mass V. Send eps and errors to zero. No additional zero-degree vertex may be inserted afterwards without repeating positivity on the enlarged graph.

Reference-only mixing fails on new zero-degree components. Fixed-edge rational density also fails: parallel cycle lengths1,sqrt2 require rational q=r sqrt2, hence q=r=0. Movable bends preserve this cycle. Exact prototype: theta=(1,1), mu=(2,0), eps=1/10; common height difference .9(2-sqrt2); slope pairs(.52,.53),(.37,.38); bends -127+90sqrt2 and -180+128sqrt2; masses189/100,9/100,1/100,1/100, total2.

Horizontal formal implication: on a complete flat actual chart, a formally étale coordinate t and bounded section p give tau=t-t(p). Suppose its residual zero fibre, after actual shrinking, is one reduced rational point. Every zero fibre modulo a^j is étale finitely presented over R/a^j. Its residual morphism is finite, so arbitrary-thickening finiteness Stacks37.3.4(2) makes the whole zero fibre finite étale. Over the local base it is free of rank1; its unit is a basis, identifying it with R/a^j compatibly through evaluation. The monic coordinate is a nonzerodivisor on the polynomial base and remains so under étale flatness. Thus tau is regular on every reduction and in the complete ring. If h evaluates to zero, h mod a^j=tau q_j uniquely; regularity makes q_j compatible and completeness gives h=tau q. Hence B/(tau)=R, the ideal is closed and Cartier, and its generic zero is ORIGINAL p. Generators of this same ideal have unit ratios and glue. Distinct smooth punctures from a meromorphic section of dL give a signed horizontal bundle with that exact generic identification; each simple section contributes one residual degree to exactly one component.

Vertical formal implication: given an ACTUAL strongly semistable node cover xy=pi_e and smooth-part overlaps where x or y is a formal unit, take integral slopes k and Gamma heights with h_w-h_v=k ell_e. Choose val(c_v)=h_v. Cartier equations are g_v=c_v and g_e=c_vx^k in the meromorphic ring. They are nonzerodivisors because xy=pi_e and base flatness. Ratios are x^k and (c_v pi_e^k/c_w)y^-k; the scalar has norm1, so these are genuine formal units. Their literal ratios satisfy the cocycle. Local frames g_i^-1 give the canonical generic section1 weight -log|g_i|, exactly h and constant on complementary fibres. On normalized residual components, the section divided by c_v has orders k and -k at the two node branches. Degree change is sum_outgoing k, counting both loop branches; total change is zero. Clear rational slopes by an integer. The twist preserves the SAME generic bundle through canonical section1. Positivity and n2 recognize an already constructed twist; a graph computation alone does not imply PSH.

Residual-field implication: for a reduced strict C-affinoid with integral canonical reduction, suppose an actual canonical chart has ring B_C^o, single Shilov point x and |H(x)^*|=|C^*|. Single-Shilov norming gives spectralnorm(f)=|f(x)|. Reduction embeds tilde B_C in tilde H(x). For a norm-one fraction f/g, choose c in C of their common value; f/c and g/c have spectral norm1, so its residue is their quotient in Frac(tilde B_C). Any norm-one element of completed H(x) is within error<1 of such a fraction, with identical residue; elements of norm<1 reduce to zero. Thus tilde H(x)=Frac(tilde B_C) through the natural map, without inferring it from fibre cardinality.

Limits: actual cofinal models, smooth/node covers and canonical-chart hypotheses still need universal verification. CLDv1 6.9.2 gives support only; raw coefficients require6.5.1/6.6.8 residual identification,6.9.3/4 coefficients and6.9.6 algebraically closed factor1, with6.9.5's calibrated-cone foundation. Those recursive applications remain incomplete. The intended formula MA(M/d)=sum deg(M|Y)/d delta_xY has neither probability normalization nor a field-degree factor; it is NOT claimed universally established here.

Put B=-E>=0, A_mu(u)=int(-u)dmu, U_mu=sup{A_mu(u):actual u in E1, sup u=0, B<=1}, and J=sup_continuous_psh(E(v)-int v dmu). The target is positive Radon of mass V, so constants cancel.

If every actual E1 test is integrable but U is infinite, choose normalized u_j with B<=1 and A_mu>=4^j. Actual convex sums w_N=sum_{j<=N}2^-j u_j+2^-N0 are nonpositive, decreasing, and have E(w_N)>=-1 by concavity. Decreasing closure gives a possibly identically-minus-infinity endpoint. O's extended majorant-energy argument excludes that endpoint BEFORE invoking E1: compactness puts a tail below any -M+1, forcing energies to minus infinity. Hence w is actual E1 with E>=-1. Sequential monotone convergence on mu gives int(-w)=sum2^-j A_mu(u_j)>=sum2^j=infinity, contradiction. No common finite-valued anchor or normalized endpoint is required.

Conversely B(tu)<=tB(u) by concavity. Take t=1 if B<=1, otherwise t=1/B. Then normalized tu has cost<=1 and tA_mu(u)<=U, giving integrability. Bounded constant shifts recover absolute integrability of every test.

Finite J implies integrability independently. Continuous v_i decreasing to actual u in E1 have a tail <=M. The dual inequality gives int(M-v_i)dmu<=MV+J-E(v_i)<=MV+J-E(u). For nonnegative continuous increasing nets on a compact Hausdorff space with Radon measure, integrals increase to the endpoint integral: directed strict open level sets, compact inner approximation and finite subcovers establish level-set masses; one common index approximates finitely many lower layer levels; truncation and refinement finish the proof. This is not arbitrary measurable-net monotone convergence. Thus u is integrable and int v_i tends to int u. O gives E(v_i) decreasing to E(u), so the functional at u is a limit of continuous values. Continuous and all-E1 suprema coincide.

Exact sharper scaling: A_k=int(-u)MA(u^[k],0^[n-k]) are finite nonnegative and sum A_k=(n+1)B. O's actual affine curvature and segment derivative give B(tu)=sum_{k=0}^n binom(n,k)A_k int_0^t s^k(1-s)^(n-k)ds. Bound the k0 term by tA0. For k>=1 use A_k<=(n+1)B and sum_{k>=1}binom(n,k)s^k(1-s)^(n-k)=1-(1-s)^n<=ns. Integration proves B(tu)<=tA0+D_n t^2B, D_n=n(n+1)/2, for EVERY real0<=t<=1.

If an ACTUAL reference bound A0<=M0 for every normalized E1 is proved, take t=[1+2M0+sqrt(2D_nB)]^-1. Linear and quadratic terms are each <=1/2, giving A_mu(u)<=U[1+2M0+sqrt(2D_nB)]. This proves finite-dual equivalence under the additional bound, not the bound's universal existence. A continuous normalized M0 estimate extends to actual endpoints using compactness sup u_i decreasing to sup u and the same Radon-net law. For curves, B(tu)=tA0+t^2(B-A0) exactly.

For an ALREADY known output mu=MA(v), O's integrability and segment concavity give E(u)<=E(v)+int(u-v)dmu. The functional is bounded above by its finite value at v. notes.text:
New draft theorem relative to the COMPLETE grants registered in n1: K is any complete real-valued non-Archimedean field with characteristic and residue characteristic zero, including trivial, nontrivial, discrete, nondiscrete and non-algebraically-closed cases. X/K is smooth geometrically integral projective of GEOMETRIC GENUS ZERO, L an ACTUAL ample rational bundle, and raw V=deg L>0. For positive Radon mu on the entire X^an, mass mu(X^an)=V plus integrability of EVERY actual E1 potential is equivalent to finite continuous-test dual J, and to mu=MA(phi) for actual all-point phi in E1. EVERY pair of solutions differs by ONE finite real constant at EVERY analytic point, including common poles. The operator is O's genuine operator. Each solution attains its actual energy-minus-integral functional by n4. Nonsplit conics are included.

First prove the norming premise. On P1 over complete algebraically closed nontrivial C, suppose an actual continuous psh reference psi has genuine curvature lambda supported on finite nonempty hyperbolic S. For continuous psh scalar f, eta=MA(psi+f) is positive of raw mass V. Choose coordinate Gauss root zeta. With q=a_y, a continuous psh metric of curvature eta has scalar p(y)=p(zeta)-int g(x,y)deta(x) relative to the standard reference. Subtract the identity for psi to obtain f(y)=f(zeta)-int g(x,y)d(eta-lambda)(x) at every hyperbolic point.

Q's actual retraction and 1-Lipschitz kernel facts make f restricted to Gamma Lipschitz, with graph Laplacian r_Gamma*eta-lambda: Delta_y g(x,y)=delta_zeta-delta_rGamma x and both measures have mass V. Put M=max_Sf and w=(f-M)_+ on Gamma. Interval Stieltjes integration by parts, including all vertex terms, gives int w d(r*eta-lambda)=-int|w'|^2. This is elementary graph calculus: f' has bounded variation from the kernel's one-jump derivatives; approximate Lipschitz w uniformly and in derivative L1, retaining endpoint values; bounded f' and finite second-derivative measure permit passage. The positive-part chain rule gives w'f'=|w'|^2 almost everywhere. Vertex terms exactly account for interval endpoints. Since w is zero on S, the left side is nonnegative, so w'=0. Connectivity gives w=0. On attached branches, g(x,y)-g(x,rGamma y)>=0 and vanishes for x in S, hence f(y)<=f(rGamma y). Continuity and Q's whole-carrier tree description recover type-I/type-IV terminals. Thus EVERY continuous psh scalar, in particular EVERY FS scalar, attains its maximum on S. For a singleton Gamma the branch argument applies directly.

For trivial valuation, T gives the theorem in its exact smooth geometrically integral projective ample domain. Suppose K is nontrivial. Put C=completed algebraic closure and G=Gal(overline K/K). Choose finite Galois E/K over which X has a point, using the finite residue field of a closed point and Galois closure in characteristic zero.

The actual splitting has an elementary proof. Flat field base change of the affine Čech complex gives H1(O)=0 and H0(O)=E. Its ACTUAL G orbit S is finite and consists of hyperbolic type-II points. Choose an original generated-multiple FS metric theta_K and invariant pullback theta_C.
